Flagship build — 01

Smart Autonomous Air Quality & Environmental Monitoring Bot

An autonomous rover that reads its environment in real time and reports it back over the air — built to go where continuous human inspection can't.

FRAME 01 / 06 CHASSIS
01 — Build

A chassis that can go anywhere

Designed and assembled a tank-track platform for uneven terrain, with an ESP32 and Arduino Uno running sensing and motion side by side.

ESP32Arduino UnoTank Chassis
02 — Drive

Power and motion, wired clean

Built the drive base around an L298N motor driver and FlySky receiver for manual override, with power and signal lines kept clean across the platform.

L298N DriverFlySky RC
03 — Circuit

One board, every sensor

Laid out a custom PCB to bring the ESP32, BMP180 and OLED onto a single, reliable board — replacing a breadboard's worth of loose wiring.

Custom PCBESP32
04 — Sense

Reading the air, continuously

Programmed acquisition from the MQ-135 air quality sensor, MQ-2 gas sensor, DHT11 and BMP180 as the rover moves through its environment.

MQ-135MQ-2DHT11BMP180
05 — Display

Live readings, on the rover

An I2C OLED shows temperature, humidity, pressure and gas status directly on the robot — no laptop required for a field check.

OLED I2C
06 — Report

Telemetry, off the rover too

Logged readings feed a ThingSpeak stream and a Power BI dashboard, turning raw sensor data into a live, remotely-viewable picture of air quality.

ThingSpeak / IoTPower BI

Why robotics

Ideas that become physical systems.

My best projects are the ones where an idea stopped being lines of code and started being a machine that could sense and act. Robotics sits exactly at the intersection I care about most — software, electronics and mechanical design.

Why NUS

An interdisciplinary bench, in a manufacturing hub.
